native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: Individuals with a criminal record (ever_jailed=1) had significantly lower wealth than those without in ALL three years: 1985, 1990, and 1996. Raw Mann-Whitney U (one-sided, jailed < non-jailed) after removing 1899 exact duplicates (10,114 rows; jailed n=239, non-jailed n=9875): 1985 U=855,564, p=1.6e-13 (jailed median 1,400 vs 6,000); 1990 U=577,663, p=6.3e-42 (300 vs 19,000); 1996 U=679,762, p=4.9e-30 (0 vs 23,700). All three survive Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (q: 1.6e-13, 1.9e-41, 7.3e-30, all < 0.05). The negative jailed effect also holds after controlling for race and sex (OLS on wealth ranks: coefs -987.7, -2095.8, -1971.2; all p < 1e-7). Caveat: ever_jailed spans 1985-1994, so the 1985 wealth snapshot may predate some respondents' incarceration, making 1985 the least clean for causal interpretation (1996 is the cleanest).
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Load data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv, drop 1899 exact duplicates (12013->10114). 2) Primary: per-year raw Mann-Whitney U (one-sided jailed<non-jailed) reporting U, p, rank-biserial r, group medians. 3) FDR Benjamini-Hochberg across the 3 years (raw + two-sided). 4) Secondary: OLS of wealth-rank ~ ever_jailed + race + sex to check direction/significance after demographic control. 5) State which years are significant and flag the 1985 temporal caveat.
